preview_en:
Two of the five winless sides left in Serie A at the start of this round meet when Parma host a Genoa side who are shy in front of goal on the road.

Match News and Current Form

Although Parma will be quick to point out that three of their opening four Serie A fixtures came against the pre-round top eight, it doesn’t negate the fact they’ve won just a single point after four rounds - their joint-worst record after matchday four in top-flight history. Conceding first in each game so far hasn’t helped their cause, nor has a lack of consistency at home, where each of their last 14 Serie A results differed from the one prior (W4, D4, L6). Drawing 1-1 at home to Monza in their last such outing would hint this game will be decided one way or another, but there’s no guarantee Parma will fall on the right side of the result here having won just two of their last 12 Sunday-held Serie A home games (D5, L5).

Genoa’s start to the campaign has been marginally worse than Parma’s as they sit below them in the table, but will perhaps be buoyed by picking up their first point of the season with last weekend’s 1-1 draw against Frosinone. They’ll certainly hope that proves to be the boost they need to see their season spark into life, as defeat here would see them post their joint-worst five-game start to a Serie A campaign in history. A disappointing nine-match winless top-flight run (D3, L6) indicates that making unwanted history is a distinct possibility here, and their misery has been most prevalent on the road where they’ve failed to score in their last four league outings (D2, L2).

Head-to-Head History

Both of last season’s meetings ended 0-0, but three Serie A victories prior for Genoa put them on a five-match unbeaten top-flight H2H run.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Parma are one of three Serie A sides pre-round yet to score before the break.

Seven of Parma’s last eight competitive games produced under 2.5 goals.

Genoa’s last seven away fixtures returned under 10.5 corners.

Eight of Genoa’s last 11 matches in all competitions featured under 2.5 goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

David Romero opened his Parma account last weekend and is surely pushing for a start having averaged 4.91 shots on target per 90 minutes in Serie A this season. Genoa’s Leo Østigård has already received three yellow cards in four Serie A games this season and was also booked in last season’s corresponding fixture.

Parma have no fresh injury concerns, but Genoa will be missing Johan Vásquez due to suspension.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With each of the last five H2Hs producing under 2.5 goals , backing a repeat outcome seems a smart approach to take.

Author: Chris Wilson
